messages:
acme_jane: Hey team — since this morning we're seeing a jump in 504s on hosted generate endpoints when clients reuse connections (HTTP/1.1 keepalive). p95 latency up and a few timeouts reported by users. Happening across two regions. Example: 30-40 504s per minute starting ~08:20 UTC.

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, thanks for the report. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK snippet)? Also which SDK version and whether you use streaming or non-streaming?

acme_jane: Repro with curl (we're not using streaming):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"input":"hello","model":"redwood/gpt-4-mini"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# we run this in a tight loop reusing keepalive connections via --keepalive
```
We saw higher failure rate when the client connection is reused for many sequential requests (concurrency=1, sequential). SDK is our in-house wrapper; we tried switching to direct curl and still saw flakes.

alex_support: Thanks. Reproduced locally with a small loop (10 req/sec) leaving connections open — got intermittent 504s after ~90s. Filing incident and escalating to SRE. @ryan_sre can you take a look at edge and ingress?

oncall_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4521.

ryan_sre: Looking at ingress logs for the customer trace ids you provided. I see a pattern: upstream read deadline exceeded on the gateway (504) and the connection group shows repeated pipelined requests on same TCP connection. Gateway logs show: 
```
2026-03-17T08:21:33Z gateway: read_chunked_body: boundary-mismatch on conn_id=8241
2026-03-17T08:21:34Z gateway: upstream_read_deadline_exceeded conn_id=8241
```
Seems like when HTTP/1.1 keepalive + naive pipelining/reuse occurs, chunked body parsing occasionally mis-aligns and leaves bytes for the next request, triggering a read timeout waiting for a new request body. That matches the customer's repro loops.

marta_eng: We haven't seen this exact boundary-mismatch in prod tests. Hypothesis: a race between connection reuse path and the chunked decoder when requests are back-to-back without an explicit `Connection: close`. We added stronger delim checks in the streaming path patch (PR #4217).

alex_support: Customer asks for a temporary mitigation while you push a fix. Any short-term workarounds?

ryan_sre: Two options that helped in our local repro:
- Client-side: set `Connection: close` or avoid reusing the same TCP connection for long tight loops
- Gateway-side temporary: disable HTTP/1.1 pipelining on the edge proxy for the customer's CIDR (we can flip a config flag)

acme_jane: We can set `Connection: close` for now, but it's a perf hit. Can you do the gateway flip?

ryan_sre: Yes, we can. I'm rolling a conservative ingress rule that forces `Connection: close` on requests from your tenant for the next 2 hours — should cut the 504s immediately. Will monitor.

oncall_bot: Change deployed to canary edge pool for tenant acme-corp. Change ID: CHG-9002.

alex_support: Noted. Customer notified.

acme_jane: Confirming — after the change we dropped to ~0-2 504s/min (was 30-40). Thanks.

marta_eng: We're preparing a patch to the chunked decoder (remove unsafe buffer reuse on connection reuse), plus an additional unit test that reproduces back-to-back requests. Targeted for a hotfix release v2026.3.18. Patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4217.

ryan_sre: Post-deploy plan: roll fix to edge proxy and runtime in two stages (canary then global) and then remove the temporary tenant rule. I'll coordinate a 2-hour maintenance window for the global rollout and post status here.

alex_support: Customer update sent — temporary mitigation in place, fix incoming, next update after canary validation.

acme_jane: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please include instructions to rollback if we see regressions.

marta_eng: Will do. Also adding a monitoring alert for boundary-mismatch error rate (new metric) so we catch regressions early.

ryan_sre: Canary started at 09:40 UTC — no spike in 5xx so far across canaries. Waiting 30m then will expand.

alex_support: Thanks all. I'll close the immediate escalation once global rollout completes and customer confirms.

oncall_bot: INC-2026-4521 status: in-progress -> resolved (temporary rule applied, patch merged to main).
